summary.headline: Kalyan Jewellers Q4 FY26 consolidated PAT rose 118% YoY to INR410 crores on 66% revenue growth to INR10,275 crores.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q4 FY26 was INR10,275 crores (up 66% YoY) and PAT was INR410 crores (up 118%), with India business PAT up 97% to INR366 crores. For FY26, consolidated revenue reached INR35,740 crores (up 43%) and PAT INR1,350 crores (up 89%). Management reported non-GML debt reduced by about INR360 crores in India, with non-GML now at INR300 crores, and Candere turned PAT positive in H2 FY26. Management said April 2026 started well despite a high base, while flagging Adhik Maas as a possible Q1 timing drag.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR28 crores YoY; PAT INR3 crores vs loss of INR12 crores

segments.name: India (Kalyan)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR8,990 crores and PBT INR495 crores (vs INR249 crores); PAT INR366 crores, up 97%. Management said India PBT margin of 5.5-5.6% is expected to stay in this range.

segments.name: Middle East
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR1,074 crores (vs INR784 crores) with PBT INR20 crores (vs INR15 crores) and PAT INR21 crores (vs INR12 crores). Four FOCO showrooms were temporarily converted to COCO to facilitate a planned Arab investor franchise deal, not yet materialised.

segments.name: Candere
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR131 crores (vs INR28 crores) and PAT INR3 crores vs loss of INR12 crores. FY26 revenue grew 160%; store-level gross margin is in the mid-30s on studded ratio above 70%. FY27 plan is 50-55 Candere stores.

guidance_outlook: Plan to open 150 showrooms in FY27 across Kalyan, Candere and the new regional brand; Candere share about 50-55 of these.
Aim to make India non-GML debt zero in FY27, possibly by H1 FY27, but management declined to guide firmly on timing.

Non-GML repayment of INR300 crores expected to save about INR30 crores in interest in FY27, at roughly 9-10%; about INR20 crores of one-off advance tax interest in FY26 adds to the reduction (around INR50 crores total).
Dividend recommended at about INR257 crores, roughly 20% of FY26 net profit, per the announced policy.
Management does not want to guide SSSG above 10% for the next 3-5 years, though recent SSSG has been 20-30%.

Gross margin expected to face YoY pressure from platinum/silver tailwinds that will not repeat; management cited about INR20 crores of silver benefit, with operating leverage and interest savings as offsets.
April 2026 started well despite a high base; Adhik Maas may shift some wedding demand between quarters, though management said revenue is not lost.
capex_capacity: Opened 129 showrooms across Kalyan and Candere in FY26, including the first Kalyan showroom in the UK.
Opened 13 stores in South India in FY26; South expansion to stay at about 13-15 showrooms, mainly in metros like Bangalore, Chennai and Hyderabad; about 60-65 showrooms planned outside South.
Middle East: 2 new showrooms opened and 5-6 renovated into bigger formats; conversion of 4 FOCO stores to COCO worth about INR200-250 crores of inventory.
Q4 showroom count rose gross by 28 but net by about 4, with management saying only one small Madurai showroom closed and the rest were relocations.
Third regional brand launch in a South state delayed until post-election situation settles.
demand_pricing: Management said SSSG for the South was lower than for non-South in Q4; non-South acceleration continued from Q3.
Akshaya Tritiya sales grew strongly; coin sales were lower than estimated this year, unlike Dhanteras when they exceeded estimates.

Management said customers buy to a rupee budget, so volumes fall as gold prices rise; gold rose about 60-70% over the past year. Consumers were pushed to studded jewellery and lower karat (22K to 18K, 18K to 14K).
Management said gold supply is not a concern, with regular bank inventory and imports via GIFT City's India International Bullion Exchange.
Gold metal loan (GML) in India is capped by bank sanctions; Middle East GML is uncapped and rises with gold prices.
Management said inventory rises by only INR30-40 for every INR100 rise in gold price, to protect ROCE.

qa_highlights.question: Why did South SSSG diverge so sharply from non-South in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said South was lower, partly because its base is higher, and non-South acceleration continued from Q3 and was more pronounced in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will non-GML debt be fully repaid by H1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to be non-GML debt free in FY27 and could do it by H1, but declined to guide on timing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost rise sequentially, and what is the underlying run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher processing charges and interest on advance tax explain the rise; about INR20 crores is one-off. Non-GML repayment should cut about INR30 crores in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 Adhik Maas period a risk to sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some sales may move between quarters, with possible slower days, but some purchases were preponed; April started well.

qa_highlights.question: How much of gross margin came from silver and platinum, and what is the FY27 impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the silver/platinum benefit was about INR20 crores and will not repeat, but operating leverage and interest savings can help. PBT margin for India should stay near 5.5-5.6%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East FOCO-to-COCO conversion's potential cash release?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only 4 showrooms were converted, worth about INR200-250 crores of inventory, and declined to budget any further conversion or cash release.

risks_watch: Gross margin sustainability after platinum and silver gains and the FOCO mix shift; Q4 gross margin reverted to about a 100 bps YoY decline in India, per an analyst.
Q1 FY27 wedding timing around Adhik Maas and tough H2 comparisons on a high base.
Middle East franchise conversion and the Arab investor deal, which is not yet materialised.
Divestment of collateral assets: INR180 crores release with disposal targeted before September 2026, and a further INR200 crores release with no timeline.
Competition from digital-only players such as BlueStone, with ad spend growth muted.
Gold price-driven volume pressure and dependence on gold metal loan limits from banks.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on Q4 and FY26 numbers and April trends, but cautious and evasive on forward guidance: management repeatedly declined to give timelines for debt repayment, Middle East conversion and the third brand, and warned against budgeting on them.
key_quotes: Q4 has been fantastic. The pickup in momentum we witnessed during the third quarter continued during the last quarter, and we ended up the financial year on an excellent note.
So, there is abundant supply of gold in the country, and we continue to receive regular inventory from our banks.
If you are trying to put a 3 to 5 -year projection, I always recommend only putting a 10% SSSG, even though I don't have a reason for it.
So the easy answer for this question will be, non-GML will be zero.

growth.why: Management plans 150 showroom openings in FY27 and guides India PBT margin at 5.5-5.6%, with non-GML debt zero targeted in FY27 (timing not firmly guided) and ~INR30 crores interest savings; no explicit revenue growth guidance, and SSSG guidance capped at 10% for 3-5 years.
